title: NanoMatAI: band gaps of 2D semiconductors from crystal structure, with a calibrated trust verdict
description:
A CGCNN ensemble that predicts the band gap of a two-dimensional monolayer from its crystal structure on CPU, together with a calibrated uncertainty interval and an explicit verdict on whether the prediction is usable.

Trained on 13 349 stable 2D semiconductors from Alexandria and evaluated on a split where no composition is shared between training and test: MAE 0.246 eV, against 0.430 eV for a composition-only baseline scored on the identical test set. The graph reads bond angles as well as bond lengths, which is what lets it separate polymorphs of one composition — 1H-MoS2 is a semiconductor and 1T-MoS2 is metallic, and a distance-only graph barely tells them apart.

Three independent out-of-domain checks decide the verdict: a metal/semiconductor gate, the spread between ensemble members, and the distance to the training set in the model's own latent space. Each exists because the previous one was caught failing on a real case. Linear heads on that latent space add a quasiparticle gap, an exciton binding energy and an absorption onset; a second ensemble adds the work function, so the band edges a contact metal is chosen on follow from the pair.

Predictions for 28 372 public 2D structures are published as a browsable static page, with a periodic-table map of where the model actually works.
